prompt:
A car speedometer displays 75 km h^-1.
(a) Explain why this instrument reading represents a scalar quantity rather than a vector quantity. [1]
(b) State what additional information is required to express the reading as a velocity. [1]

answer.text:
(a) The speedometer indicates speed, which has magnitude and unit only without any direction of travel.
(b) The direction of travel (e.g. north, east, or a bearing) is required.

mark_scheme: Part (a) [1 mark]: Speed has magnitude only / no direction is displayed.
hints: Does a speedometer show which way the car is pointing?
solution:
(a) The speedometer reading gives magnitude and unit only, with no direction of travel; therefore it is a scalar.
(b) Direction of motion (e.g. compass direction or bearing) is required to state the velocity.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Part (a): recognize speed has magnitude only (1 mark).
Step 2: Part (b): state direction of travel (1 mark).
lesson_anchors: A scalar is complete without a direction
A common mistake: the unit or the story does not decide
exclusions: vector addition and resolution deferred to l11
